lessons.title: Candlesticks and trends
lessons.summary: Reading a price chart one candle at a time.

cards.title: One candle
cards.body: Each candle shows a time slot: where the price opened, its highest and lowest points, and where it closed. Green = closed higher than it opened; red = closed lower.

cards.title: Timeframes
cards.body: A 1-minute chart shows tiny moves; a 15-minute chart shows the bigger picture. The same moment can look like a crash on one and a blip on another.

cards.title: Trends
cards.body: Higher highs and higher lows = uptrend. Lower highs and lower lows = downtrend. Trends end without warning — a chart shows the past, not the future.

quiz.question: A green candle means…
options: The price closed higher than it opened
quiz.explanation: Colour shows direction within that time slot.

quiz.question: The thin lines above and below a candle show…
options: The high and low of that period

quiz.question: Can a chart tell you what the price will do next?
options: No — it shows what already happened
quiz.explanation: Patterns can fail at any time.

lessons.title: Support, resistance, stop-loss
lessons.summary: Planning your exit before you enter.

cards.title: Support and resistance
cards.body: Support is a price where buying has often stopped falls; resistance is where selling has often stopped rises. They're areas, not exact lines, and they break.

cards.title: Stop-loss
cards.body: A stop-loss sells automatically if the price falls to a level you choose. It caps how much one bad trade can cost.

cards.title: Take-profit
cards.body: A take-profit sells automatically at a gain you choose, so you don't get greedy and watch a profit vanish.

cards.title: Drag the lines
cards.body: In the simulator you can drag the red stop-loss and green take-profit lines on the chart once you have a position.

quiz.question: What does a stop-loss do?
options: Sells automatically if the price falls to your level
quiz.explanation: It limits the loss from one trade.

quiz.question: You buy at Rs 100 with a stop-loss at Rs 95. The price falls to Rs 94. What happens?
options: Your position is sold around Rs 95 or just below
The trade is cancelled with no loss
quiz.explanation: The stop triggers once the level is crossed.

quiz.question: Support levels are…
options: Areas where falls have often paused before

lessons.title: Position size and risk/reward
lessons.summary: How much to risk on one idea.

cards.title: The 2% rule
cards.body: Many professionals risk at most 1–2% of their account on one trade. With Rs 100,000, a stop-loss should cost no more than Rs 2,000 if hit.

cards.title: Sizing a position
cards.body: Risk per unit = entry − stop-loss. Units = money you're willing to lose ÷ risk per unit. Rs 2,000 ÷ Rs 5 = 400 units.

cards.title: Risk/reward
cards.body: If you risk Rs 5 to aim for Rs 10, that's 1:2. Good traders still lose often — they just make sure winners are bigger than losers.

cards.title: Fees eat profits
cards.body: Each trade here costs 0.2% (min Rs 25). Twenty small trades a day can cost more than they earn.

quiz.question: Account Rs 100,000, 2% rule. Max loss on one trade?
Entry Rs 50, stop Rs 48, willing to lose Rs 1,000. How many units?
Why do fees matter more in short-term trading?
options: You pay them on every trade, and trades are frequent
quiz.explanation: Small fees × many trades = big cost.

lessons.title: Emotions and why most traders lose
lessons.summary: The honest truth about short-term trading.

cards.title: Most lose
cards.body: Studies of retail day traders in several countries find that the large majority lose money over time, and only a tiny share earn more than a basic wage.

cards.title: Revenge trading
cards.body: After a loss, it's tempting to trade bigger to 'win it back'. This is how small losses become big ones. Walk away instead.

cards.title: Loss limits
cards.body: Decide a daily loss limit before you start. In the trainer, trading pauses if you lose 20% of your wallet in a day.

cards.title: Take breaks
cards.body: Hours of staring at ticks wears down judgement. The trainer nudges you to take a break after 30 minutes.

quiz.question: What does research say about most retail day traders?
quiz.explanation: Fees, spreads and emotions work against them.

quiz.question: You just lost Rs 5,000. What's 'revenge trading'?
options: Making a bigger, rushed trade to win it back

quiz.question: A good response to hitting your daily loss limit is…
quiz.explanation: Limits only work if you respect them.

lessons.title: Spotting trading scams
lessons.summary: Fixed returns, binary options and pressure tactics.

cards.title: Guaranteed returns
cards.body: Any platform promising fixed daily or monthly returns from trading is a red flag. Real trading can always lose money.

cards.title: Binary options
cards.body: "Will the price be up or down in 60 seconds?" apps pay less than double your stake on a win, so even a 50/50 guess loses over time. Try the Up-or-Down game to see it.

cards.title: Check the licence
cards.body: In Sri Lanka, the SEC licenses stockbrokers and the Central Bank regulates deposit-takers. Unregulated forex apps and recruit-a-friend schemes are not protected; pyramid schemes are illegal.

cards.title: Pressure tactics
cards.body: "Only today", "deposit more to unlock your profits", or a stranger teaching you to trade on WhatsApp — walk away.

quiz.question: An app promises a guaranteed 2% profit every day from forex trading. This is…
quiz.explanation: No genuine trading can guarantee returns.

quiz.question: A 60-second up/down app pays 1.8× on a win. If you guess 50/50, over time you…
options: Lose about 10% of what you stake
quiz.explanation: 0.5 × 1.8 = 0.9: you get back 90% of stakes on average.

quiz.question: Who licenses stockbrokers in Sri Lanka?
quiz.explanation: Check the SEC's list before trusting a broker.

quiz.question: A stranger on WhatsApp offers to teach you trading and asks you to deposit on a new app. You should…
quiz.explanation: This is a common scam pattern.
